content.text: This is unexpected, and in my estimation, incorrect behavior because xsd:dateTime can represent a time before the epoch.
It causes problems, because after transforming a resource for the purpose of indexing, solr may expect to index a dateTime field type and receives a long which is unexpected.
I tested this and can verify everything works as expected.  xsd:dateTimes appear instead of longs, and solr is happy.  It's able to index the LDPath xsd:dateTime fields as Solr date fields.
?, do you have time to quickly do a code-review of this PR?
After depositing the attached LDPath document to '/fedora:system/fedora:transform/fedora:ldpath/fedora-tx/fedora:Container', invoking this transform on a typical Fedora resource produces output like:
Note that the xsd:dateTime fields are transformed to longs.

comments.body:
This is unexpected, and in my estimation, incorrect behavior because xsd:dateTime can represent a time before the epoch.

It causes problems, because after transforming a resource for the purpose of indexing, solr may expect to index a dateTime field type and receives a long which is unexpected.
Elliot Metsger, can you verify this patch?

Andrew Woods I tested this and can verify everything works as expected. xsd:dateTimes appear instead of longs, and solr is happy. It's able to index the LDPath xsd:dateTime fields as Solr date fields.

Thanks, Elliot Metsger.
Esmé Cowles?, do you have time to quickly do a code-review of this PR?
